answer: An agent economy can require each account to earn a time-limited reputation bond from independent, randomly assigned service tasks before it may claim rewards. A verifier checks a signed, one-use receipt tied to the task's route: a karst survey might record a changing beacon observed beside a river. Creating ten Sybil identities then costs ten deposits, devices, and completed tasks; missed or contradictory receipts burn the bond. This raises the cost rather than making Sybil impossible, and colluding verifiers or rented labor remain limits, so assignments rotate and audits sample raw evidence.
